correctness.rationale: All \(q\ge3\), \(n\ge2\), labeled circular windows and rotation equivalence are defined. Three balanced missing edges decompose into loops, a 2-cycle plus loop, or a primitive 3-cycle. BEST reduces necklace counting to factorial weights and in-arborescence cofactors; the directed matrix-tree theorem reduces each ratio to a 2-by-2 or 3-by-3 determinant, including an essential extra one-letter-overlap term for a repeated-symbol 3-cycle. The \(n=2\) degree collision case is enumerated separately. Cofactors are positive for the stipulated \(q,n\), ensuring Eulerian connectivity. Symbolic expansion of the exceptional determinants checked for all three \(n-1\) residue classes. The standalone full graph verifier independently evaluated all 212 balanced missing-edge sets for six \((q,n)\) pairs, and direct ternary \(n=2\) necklace enumeration returned 20. Finite verification supplements, rather than replaces, the infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A general Eulerian-subgraph matrix-tree formula is classical and is logically broader as a method, but it does not give the claimed explicit four structural classes, their q/n-dependent tree ratios, or the summation without nontrivial overlap calculations. The stronger special P-sequence condition counts a proper subset and cannot imply this total.

originality.rationale: The target \(q\ge3\), \(n\ge2\), exactly three missing length-n windows is a natural unresolved near-power generalized-de-Bruijn enumeration family. Relevant full-text sources give the definition, shorter deletion existence, and a stricter analogue, but not a statement implying the present exact all-order count; no matching published result appeared under six meaning-based targeted queries. The period-three repeated-symbol rank-three determinant correction and full four-class count are absent from the examined works. Residual unindexed-source risk remains.
residual_risks: A not-fully-indexed earlier enumeration in universal-cycle, feedback-shift-register, or graph-arborescence literature might express the same specialization.
The nonbinary \(q^n-2\) result is adjacent work but does not directly imply the primitive period-three cases.
The order-two ternary data point is known and is not claimed as independent novelty.

value.rationale: The guiding generalized de Bruijn literature explicitly identifies exact counting close to q-power lengths as an open mathematical question. This theorem gives an infinite \(q\ge3\), \(n\ge2\) closed formula at defect three, completely classifies admissible three-word deletions, and isolates a nontrivial repeated-symbol periodic-overlap correction. The classification serves the natural enumeration problem rather than an arbitrary isolated numerical slice. It does not claim binary or P-sequence extensions.
